title: Country Sourdough Boule
description: Country Sourdough Boule made from a small batch of scratch dough.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Combine {bf}, {starter}, {water}, {salt}. Fold until the flour is moist. Cover for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Build strength
steps.text: Fold each side of the dough toward the center. Repeat every 30 minutes for three rounds.

steps.title: Bulk ferment
steps.text: Keep covered at 72–75°F for another 2–5 hours, until puffy and about 50% larger. Temperature and starter activity govern the timing.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Gather the dough into a taut ball with a bench scraper; proof seam up in a floured towel-lined bowl.

steps.title: Proof
steps.text: Cover and proof 60–120 minutes until puffy; a light fingertip dent should return slowly.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the Samsung oven to 450°F on conventional Bake.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Use a parchment-lined small Dutch oven with a heat-rated lid. Score a deep slash. Bake covered for 22 minutes and finish uncovered. Allow 34–39 minutes; verify 205°F at the center.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool on a rack for 60 minutes before slicing.

notes: Make ahead: weigh the dry ingredients the evening before. Use a bubbly starter that doubles after feeding, maintained with equal weights of flour and water. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Cool completely and freeze sliced or individually wrapped for up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: wrap a serving in a damp towel and microwave for 15–25 seconds. Freezer reheat: thaw wrapped, then warm the same way. Serve with soup or gravy for a softer bite. Allow about 5–9 hours for fermentation and proofing in addition to mixing and baking. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/8 of recipe): 134 kcal, 4.9 g protein, 26.9 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 1.2 g fiber, 197 mg sodium. To build starter from scratch: mix 20 g King Arthur whole wheat flour with 20 g water in a clean jar and cover loosely. After 24 hours retain 20 g and feed 20 g water and 20 g all-purpose flour. Repeat daily; when active, feed every 12 hours until it doubles reliably within 6–8 hours, often 7–14 days. Once active, mix 25 g starter with 50 g water and 50 g flour; weigh the recipe amount at its peak. Feeding discard is outside the recipe yield.
